sections.h2: Old cabinets often have solid wood
body: Older kitchens often have something newer ones don't: solid wood boxes and doors that are still square, even if the finish is worn out. Replacing them can mean tearing out countertops and backsplash for cabinets that may not be as sturdy. Cabinet refinishing in High Springs, FL keeps the solid wood and updates the color. The same approach works on builder cabinets in Bridlewood or Bailey Estates when the layout works but the stain looks dated.

During the walkthrough, we check for water damage under the sink, loose face frames, and doors that won't close flat. Problems like these are noted in the estimate so you know whether refinishing will hold up.

sections.h2: If a past paint job is peeling
body: We often get called to fix cabinets someone painted with wall paint and no primer, and now it's peeling at every handle. Our article on temporary fixes for peeling cabinet paint can help in the meantime. The real fix is stripping or sanding back to a sound surface, then applying a primer that actually bonds.

bullets: Label and remove doors, drawers, and hardware
Degrease thoroughly, since cooking oil is the main reason cabinet paint fails
Sand to dull the old finish, then remove all dust
Prime with a bonding primer suited to the wood or old finish
Apply two coats of waterborne urethane enamel, which cures hard without yellowing like oil
Rehang, adjust, and walk the finished kitchen with you

body: Older homes often have built-in china cabinets, bookcases, and linen closets that can be refinished in the same color or a coordinating one. Bath vanities follow the same process. We can match a color from a chip or an existing door. For help choosing, book a color session in High Springs. If the kitchen walls need work too, add them through interior painting. The schedule, including which days doors are off, is in the written estimate. Our main cabinet refinishing page covers the process in more depth, and the High Springs page has everything else.

faqs.q: Is it worth painting old solid-wood cabinets?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Solid wood boxes that are square and dry are a good base for paint. We point out any water damage or loose frames during the walkthrough so you can decide.

faqs.q: Why did my previous painted cabinets peel?
faqs.a: The most common causes are grease left on the surface, no bonding primer, and wall paint used instead of an enamel. Fixing it means getting back to a sound surface and starting over with the right products.

faqs.q: Can I keep using my kitchen during the work?
faqs.a: Mostly. The kitchen stays usable for much of the project, though counters need to be cleared. The estimate includes the full schedule.

faqs.q: Do you paint built-in shelving and bookcases?
faqs.a: Yes. Built-ins, vanities, and laundry cabinets use the same prep and enamel system and can go on the same estimate.
